page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dlsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 480 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 48 KB of L1d cache. Memory capacity is configured at 192.0 GB, which yields a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and vector processing capabilities. The server achieved a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 104,787.21 and a strong multi-core stress-ng CPU performance of 95,440.36. Single-threaded performance is also notable, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,224.0 and a top-tier gzip compression rate of 36.54 GB/sec. The processor supports Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which reflected in top-tier scores for extended instructions and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth is strong, reaching 333.72 GB/sec for large block read-only operations, though the overall PassMark memory score remains in the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of the D96ls_v7 is its low memory density relative to its high compute capacity, making it less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale in-memory caching. However, this resource allocation provides qualitative cost efficiency for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive RAM footprints. The server demonstrates high throughput in static web serving (142.01 GB/sec) and Redis SET operations (151.03 million operations/sec). It is also highly capable for medium-model LLM inference prompt processing (304.72 tokens/sec) and software compilation. Appropriate workloads include compute-bound tasks, web serving, cryptography, and parallelized CPU-based simulation.

It features 192.0 GB of system memory, establishing a low 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. The server lacks local storage and GPUs but is Premium Storage capable. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier performance in multi-threaded decompression, cryptography, and CPU-based ray tracing, supported by hardware-accelerated AVX-512 and AMX instructions. While memory capacity is constrained relative to the massive compute footprint, the instance delivers strong memory bandwidth and exceptional Redis SET throughput. The D96ls_v7 is suited for compute-intensive workloads, software compilation, high-throughput web serving, and medium-scale language model prompt processing.
